{{short description|American condensed matter physicist (born 1961)}}
{{about|the American physicist|the Swedish orienteer|Karin Rabe}}

{{Use mdy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=October 2020}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=October 2020}}
'''Karin Maria Rabe'''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rabe |first=Karin Maria |date=1987 |title=Ab initio statistical mechanics of structural phase transitions |url=https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/05713905-6f6d-458a-b845-8d5d642eb3e2 |website=Massachusetts Institute of Technology}}</ref> (born April 1, 1961){{r|cv}} is an American [[Condensed matter physics|condensed matter]] and [[Computational materials science|computational materials]] physicist known for her studies of materials near phase transitions, including [[ferroelectricity|ferroelectrics]], [[multiferroics]], and [[martensite]]s.{{r|amacad|nas}} She also works on the theoretical design of new materials.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Karin M. Rabe |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/karin-m-rabe-gkynv1/ |access-date=2023-05-31 |website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> She is a distinguished professor and Board of Governors Professor of Physics at [[Rutgers University]].{{r|profile}}  

==Education and career==
Rabe was born in New York City and attended the [[Bronx High School of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rabe |first=Karin M. |title=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/karin-m-rabe-gkynv1/ |url= |website=National Academy of Sciences}}</ref> She graduated ''[[Latin honors|magna cum laude]]'' from [[Princeton University]] in 1982, with a bachelor's degree in physics. She completed her Ph.D. in 1987 at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]; her dissertation ''Ab initio Statistical Mechanics of Structural Phase Transitions'' was supervised by [[John Joannopoulos]].{{r|cv|adler2}}

After postdoctoral research at [[AT&T Bell Laboratories]], she joined [[Yale University]] as Clare Boothe Luce Assistant Professor of Applied Physics and Physics in 1989. She became full professor at Yale in 1999, and moved to Rutgers in 2000.{{r|cv|adler2}} At Rutgers, her doctoral students have included 2013 [[MacArthur Fellows Program|MacArthur "Genius" Award]] winner [[Craig Fennie]].{{r|fennie}}

Rabe also served as chair of the board of the [[Aspen Center for Physics]] from 2018 to 2021, as president from 2013 to 2016, and as vice president from 2007 to 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aspen Center for Physics |date=2021 |title=Past Board Chairs and Officers," Aspen Center for Physics |url=https://www.aspenphys.org/aboutus/governance/board/pastofficers.html |access-date=2023-05-31 |website=www.aspenphys.org }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Recognition==
Rabe was named Board of Governors Professor by Rutgers in 2013.{{r|bog}}

In 2002, she was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] (APS), after a nomination from the APS Division of Materials Physics "for fundamental contributions to the development and application of theoretical and computational methods for the study of structural phase transitions in solids".{{r|faps}} Rabe won the [[David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics]] for 2008 "for research, writings and presentations on the theory of structural phase transitions and for the application of first-principles electronic structure methods to the understanding of technologically important phenomena in ferroelectrics".{{r|adler|adler2}}

She was named a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2011,{{r|aaas}} and elected to both the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2013.{{r|amacad|nas}}

== Research ==
Rabe’s research has focused on the computational analysis of the physics of crystalline solids using first-principles. She has examined material systems which are close to structural, electronic, and magnetic phase transitions. Such systems include [[Ferroelectricity|ferroelectrics]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Seleznev |first1=Daniel |last2=Singh |first2=Sobhit |last3=Bonini |first3=John |last4=Rabe |first4=Karin M. |last5=Vanderbilt |first5=David |date=May 2, 2023 |title=Cyclic Ferroelectric Switching and Quantized Charge Transport in CuInP<sub>2</sub>S<sub>6</sub> |journal=Physical Review B |volume=108 |issue=18 |article-number=L180101 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.108.L180101 |arxiv=2305.01182 |bibcode=2023PhRvB.108r0101S }}</ref> [[Antiferroelectricity|antiferroelectrics]], [[Piezoelectricity|piezoelectrics]], [[High-κ dielectric|high-k dielectrics]], [[multiferroics]], shape-memory compounds, magnetic and nonmagnetic [[Martensite|martensites]]. These materials exhibit properties which support a wide range of technological applications, including information and energy storage and conversion.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-08-14 |title=Karin Rabe |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/people/karin-rabe/ |access-date=2023-05-31 |website=Simons Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref>

Rabe’s research has also examined the effects of epitaxial strain and the properties of interfaces in thin films, superlattices,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-25 |title=Karin M. Rabe |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/karin-m-rabe |access-date=2023-05-31 |website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences |language=en}}</ref> and other artificially structured systems.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Du |first1=Dongxue |last2=Manzo |first2=Sebastian |last3=Zhang |first3=Chenyu |last4=Saraswat |first4=Vivek |last5=Genser |first5=Konrad T. |last6=Rabe |first6=Karin M. |last7=Voyles |first7=Paul M. |last8=Arnold |first8=Michael S. |last9=Kawasaki |first9=Jason K. |date=2021-05-03 |title=Epitaxy, exfoliation, and strain-induced magnetism in rippled Heusler membranes |journal=Nature Communications |volume=12 |issue=1 |pages=2494 |doi=10.1038/s41467-021-22784-y  |doi-access=free|pmid=33941781 |pmc=8093223 |arxiv=2006.10100 |bibcode=2021NatCo..12.2494D |issn=2041-1723}}</ref> 

Finally, Rabe has applied first-principles approaches to theoretically design new materials with optimized or useful properties, as well as to discover new classes of functional materials.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-08-14 |title=Karin Rabe |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/people/karin-rabe/ |access-date=2023-05-31 |website=Simons Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref>
